extracted.intended_audience: corporate management and sustainability/reporting professionals preparing ESG/IFRS sustainability disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for companies on using and aligning corporate sustainability (ESG) disclosures with the SASB Standards and the ISSB/IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. Covers why SASB is useful, how it fits with other frameworks, ISSB maintenance, and recommended next steps for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-specific focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The SASB Standards identify sustainability disclosure topics that are reasonably likely to be relevant within each of 77 different industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the industry-specific guidance and metrics rather than generic topics — SASB's unique, industry-specific focus is central to providing relevant disclosure for a given sector. Leverage the industry matrix to identify the most relevant topics for your company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor relevance / financially material topics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Standards were developed from extensive outreach with companies and investors to understand the information investors needed and are designed to determine a company’s financially material sustainability topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying material ESG topics, prioritize those reasonably likely to affect financial performance or investor decision-making. Treat SASB as the primary input for investor-focused materiality assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused, mostly quantitative metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB Standards include a small number of focused, mostly quantitative, metrics to capture performance on each topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concise, measurable metrics for disclosures to enable comparability and to meet investor needs; avoid overly broad qualitative lists when following SASB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and comparability of disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB Standards are designed to provide consistent and comparable disclosures that meet investor needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the prescribed metrics and topic definitions consistently year-to-year and across peer companies to support comparability. Companies addressing a broader audience should supplement SASB to preserve comparability for investor uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundational input to ISSB/IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: With the creation of the ISSB, the SASB Standards now serve as a foundational building block for the new global standards; the ISSB's first two standards contain industry requirements and directly refer to guidance that is either in the SASB Standards or derived from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat SASB alignment as preparatory work for IFRS S1 and S2 adoption; map existing SASB disclosures to expected ISSB/IFRS requirements to streamline compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to refer to SASB in IFRS S1
rubrics_metrics.description: In IFRS S1, companies will be required to refer to and consider the SASB Standards when identifying relevant sustainability-related risks and opportunities to report, and when selecting disclosures applicable to those risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate SASB into your IFRS S1 materiality and disclosure-selection process — explicitly document how SASB guidance was considered and used to select disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of climate-related industry requirements with SASB (IFRS S2)
rubrics_metrics.description: IFRS S2 includes industry-based disclosure requirements and guidance for fulfilling those requirements; this content was derived from and is aligned with the climate-related content in the SASB Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SASB climate metrics and industry guidance as a direct input when preparing disclosures under IFRS S2 to ensure alignment with climate-related disclosure expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to address US-specific references and enhance global relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISSB has been addressing concerns that the SASB Standards include some US-specific references and has committed to carry forward projects aimed at enhancing the relevance of certain industry standards (e.g., alternative proteins, single-use plastics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review SASB provisions for any jurisdiction-specific references and monitor ISSB updates that internationalize or adapt SASB content; adjust disclosures where necessary for local regulatory contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementing SASB with stakeholder-focused frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the SASB Standards are designed to meet investor needs, companies that want to speak to a broader range of stakeholders would also need to look to other standards such as the GRI or the EU's CSRD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine SASB (investor-focused) disclosures with GRI/CSRD or sector-specific EU standards when your reporting aims to address non-investor stakeholders (e.g., communities, employees, regulators). Map overlaps and gaps between frameworks to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing maintenance and enhancement by the ISSB
rubrics_metrics.description: The SASB Standards are maintained and enhanced by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) following consolidation into the IFRS Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect continuing updates to metrics and topics; establish processes to track ISSB releases and incorporate standard updates into your reporting cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical next steps for reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended actions: keep reporting under SASB; see KPMG's ISSB Standards digital hub; speak to local KPMG contacts; review the ISSB's website; consider responding to the ISSB's consultation; consider SASB's materiality finder; engage in industry working groups; keep using or investigate how to start using SASB Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these concrete steps to maintain alignment, influence the standard-setting process, and get support: use materiality tools, consult experts, participate in consultations and industry groups, and continue or begin SASB-aligned reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SASB to promote efficient resource allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB reporting facilitates identification of material ESG topics for your industry and therefore can promote efficient resource allocation for corporate sustainability efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage SASB-based materiality results to prioritize sustainability investments and reporting efforts toward financially material issues.
